f.title: Establish, document, implement and maintain a risk management system
f.statement: Manufacturers shall establish, document, implement and maintain a system for risk management as described in Section 3 of Annex I.
f.applicability: Medical devices (and Annex XVI products) placed on the Union market

f.title: Conduct clinical evaluation including post-market clinical follow-up (PMCF)
f.statement: Manufacturers shall conduct a clinical evaluation in accordance with the requirements set out in Article 61 and Annex XIV, including a PMCF.

f.title: Quality management system must cover PMS, vigilance reporting, CAPA and data analysis processes
f.statement: The quality management system shall address at least, among other aspects: setting-up, implementation and maintenance of a post-market surveillance system in accordance with Article 83; handling communication with competent authorities, notified bodies, other economic operators, customers and/or other stakeholders; processes for reporting of serious incidents and field safety corrective actions in the context of vigilance; management of corrective and preventive actions and verification of their effectiveness; and processes for monitoring and measurement of output, data analysis and product improvement.
f.applicability: Medical devices (and Annex XVI products) placed on the Union market

f.title: Implement and keep up to date the post-market surveillance system

f.title: Take immediate corrective action, withdrawal or recall for non-conforming devices and inform distributors
f.statement: Manufacturers who consider or have reason to believe that a device which they have placed on the market or put into service is not in conformity with this Regulation shall immediately take the necessary corrective action to bring that device into conformity, to withdraw it or to recall it, as appropriate. They shall inform the distributors of the device in question and, where applicable, the authorised representative and importers accordingly.
f.applicability: Medical devices (and Annex XVI products) placed on the Union market
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Quality system & CAPA

They shall inform the distributors of the device in question and, where applicable, the authorised representative and importers accordingly.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves the whole statement. Confirmed.

f.title: Immediately inform competent authorities and notified body when a non-conforming device presents a serious risk
f.statement: Where the device presents a serious risk, manufacturers shall immediately inform the competent authorities of the Member States in which they made the device available and, where applicable, the notified body that issued a certificate for the device in accordance with Article 56, in particular, of the non-compliance and of any corrective action taken.
f.applicability: Non-conforming devices presenting a serious risk

f.title: Have a system for recording and reporting incidents and field safety corrective actions
f.statement: Manufacturers shall have a system for recording and reporting of incidents and field safety corrective actions as described in Articles 87 and 88.

f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Case processing & follow-up

f.title: Provide conformity information on request and cooperate with competent authorities on corrective actions
f.statement: Manufacturers shall, upon request by a competent authority, provide it with all the information and documentation necessary to demonstrate the conformity of the device, in an official Union language determined by the Member State concerned. The competent authority of the Member State of the registered place of business may require free samples or access to the device. Manufacturers shall cooperate with a competent authority, at its request, on any corrective action taken to eliminate or, if that is not possible, mitigate the risks posed by devices which they have placed on the market or put into service.
f.applicability: Medical devices (and Annex XVI products) placed on the Union market

Manufacturers shall cooperate with a competent authority, at its request, on any corrective action taken to eliminate or, if that is not possible, mitigate the risks posed by devices which they have placed on the market or put into service.

f.title: Have at least one person responsible for regulatory compliance (PRRC) with the requisite expertise
f.statement: Manufacturers shall have available within their organisation at least one person responsible for regulatory compliance who possesses the requisite expertise in the field of medical devices, demonstrated by either (a) a university degree or recognised equivalent in law, medicine, pharmacy, engineering or another relevant scientific discipline plus at least one year of professional experience in regulatory affairs or quality management systems relating to medical devices, or (b) four years of such professional experience.

f.applicability: Medical devices (and Annex XVI products) placed on the Union market

f.title: Sponsor: fully record critical adverse events, SAEs, device deficiencies and new findings in clinical investigations
f.statement: The sponsor shall fully record: any adverse event of a type identified in the clinical investigation plan as being critical to the evaluation of the results; any serious adverse event; any device deficiency that might have led to a serious adverse event if appropriate action had not been taken, intervention had not occurred, or circumstances had been less fortunate; and any new findings in relation to any of those events.
f.clause: Article 80(1) Recording and reporting of adverse events that occur during clinical investigations
f.applicability: Clinical investigations of devices under the Regulation (other than PMCF investigations, see Art 80(5)-(6))
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

f.title: Sponsor: report related SAEs, device deficiencies and new findings without delay to all Member States via the electronic system
f.statement: The sponsor shall report, without delay, to all Member States in which the clinical investigation is being conducted, by means of the electronic system referred to in Article 73: any serious adverse event that has a causal relationship with the investigational device, the comparator or the investigation procedure or where such causal relationship is reasonably possible; any device deficiency that might have led to a serious adverse event if appropriate action had not been taken, intervention had not occurred, or circumstances had been less fortunate; and any new findings in relation to those events. The period for reporting shall take account of the severity of the event. Where necessary to ensure timely reporting, the sponsor may submit an initial report that is incomplete followed up by a complete report.
f.clause: Article 80(2) Recording and reporting of adverse events that occur during clinical investigations

f.title: Plan, establish and maintain a post-market surveillance system for each device as part of the QMS
f.statement: For each device, manufacturers shall plan, establish, document, implement, maintain and update a post-market surveillance system in a manner that is proportionate to the risk class and appropriate for the type of device. That system shall be an integral part of the manufacturer's quality management system referred to in Article 10(9).

f.statement: The post-market surveillance system shall be suited to actively and systematically gathering, recording and analysing relevant data on the quality, performance and safety of a device throughout its entire lifetime, and to drawing the necessary conclusions and to determining, implementing and monitoring any preventive and corrective actions.

f.title: Use PMS data to update benefit-risk, risk management, labelling, clinical evaluation, SSCP and to detect trends; update technical documentation
f.statement: Data gathered by the manufacturer's post-market surveillance system shall in particular be used: to update the benefit-risk determination and improve risk management; to update the design and manufacturing information, the instructions for use and the labelling; to update the clinical evaluation; to update the summary of safety and clinical performance (Article 32); to identify needs for preventive, corrective or field safety corrective action; to identify options to improve usability, performance and safety; when relevant, to contribute to post-market surveillance of other devices; and to detect and report trends in accordance with Article 88. The technical documentation shall be updated accordingly.

f.title: Class IIa, IIb and III devices: prepare a PSUR per device or group with required content
f.statement: Manufacturers of class IIa, class IIb and class III devices shall prepare a periodic safety update report (PSUR) for each device and where relevant for each category or group of devices, summarising the results and conclusions of the analyses of the post-market surveillance data gathered under the PMS plan together with a rationale and description of any preventive and corrective actions taken. Throughout the lifetime of the device, the PSUR shall set out: the conclusions of the benefit-risk determination; the main findings of the PMCF; and the volume of sales of the device and an estimate evaluation of the size and other characteristics of the population using the device and, where practicable, the usage frequency of the device.

f.statement: Manufacturers of class IIb and class III devices shall update the PSUR at least annually. That PSUR shall, except in the case of custom-made devices, be part of the technical documentation as specified in Annexes II and III.

f.title: Report serious incidents and field safety corrective actions to competent authorities via the electronic system
f.statement: Manufacturers of devices made available on the Union market, other than investigational devices, shall report to the relevant competent authorities, in accordance with Articles 92(5) and (7): (a) any serious incident involving devices made available on the Union market, except expected side-effects which are clearly documented in the product information and quantified in the technical documentation and are subject to trend reporting under Article 88; and (b) any field safety corrective action in respect of devices made available on the Union market, including any FSCA undertaken in a third country for a device also legally made available on the Union market, if the reason is not limited to the device made available in the third country. The reports shall be submitted through the electronic system referred to in Article 92.
f.clause: Article 87(1) Reporting of serious incidents and field safety corrective actions
f.applicability: Devices made available on the Union market; FSCAs in third countries where the reason is not limited to the third-country device
f.exceptions: Expected side-effects clearly documented in the product information, quantified in the technical documentation and subject to trend reporting under Article 88.
f.systems: Electronic system on vigilance and post-market surveillance (Article 92)

rows.quote:
1.   Manufacturers of devices made available on the Union market, other than investigational devices, shall report, to the relevant competent authorities, in accordance with Articles 92(5) and (7), the following:

 (a)

 any serious incident involving devices made available on the Union market, except expected side-effects which are clearly documented in the product information and quantified in the technical documentation and are subject to trend reporting pursuant to Article 88;

 (b)

 any field safety corrective action in respect of devices made available on the Union market, including any field safety corrective action undertaken in a third country in relation to a device which is also legally made available on the Union market, if the reason for the field safety corrective action is not limited to the device made available in the third country.

 The reports referred to in the first subparagraph shall be submitted through the electronic system referred to in Article 92.

systems: Electronic system on vigilance and post-market surveillance (Article 92)

f.statement: As a general rule, the period for the reporting of serious incidents and field safety corrective actions shall take account of the severity of the serious incident.

f.title: Report serious incidents immediately once causality is established or reasonably possible and no later than 15 days
f.statement: Manufacturers shall report any serious incident immediately after they have established the causal relationship between that incident and their device or that such causal relationship is reasonably possible and not later than 15 days after they become aware of the incident.

f.title: Report death or unanticipated serious deterioration in health immediately and no later than 10 days

f.statement: If, after becoming aware of a potentially reportable incident, the manufacturer is uncertain about whether the incident is reportable, it shall nevertheless submit a report within the timeframe required in accordance with paragraphs 2 to 5.

f.title: Report field safety corrective actions without undue delay in advance of undertaking them
f.statement: Except in cases of urgency in which the manufacturer needs to undertake field safety corrective action immediately, the manufacturer shall, without undue delay, report the field safety corrective action in advance of the field safety corrective action being undertaken.
f.exceptions: Cases of urgency in which the FSCA must be undertaken immediately.

f.title: Periodic summary reports may replace individual reports for similar serious incidents if agreed with the coordinating authority
f.statement: For similar serious incidents that occur with the same device or device type and for which the root cause has been identified or a field safety corrective action implemented or where the incidents are common and well documented, the manufacturer may provide periodic summary reports instead of individual serious incident reports, on condition that the coordinating competent authority, in consultation with the competent authorities concerned, has agreed with the manufacturer on the format, content and frequency of the periodic summary reporting. Where a single competent authority is concerned, the manufacturer may provide periodic summary reports following agreement with that competent authority.
f.applicability: Similar serious incidents with the same device or device type with identified root cause, implemented FSCA, or common and well-documented incidents
f.exceptions: Requires prior agreement on format, content and frequency with the coordinating competent authority (or the single competent authority concerned).

f.title: On incidents forwarded by a competent authority, report serious incidents or provide an explanatory statement
f.statement: Where the manufacturer of the device concerned considers that the incident is a serious incident, it shall provide a report in accordance with Article 87(1) to (5) to the competent authority of the Member State in which that serious incident occurred and shall take the appropriate follow-up action in accordance with Article 89. Where the manufacturer considers that the incident is not a serious incident or is an expected undesirable side-effect covered by trend reporting, it shall provide an explanatory statement. If the competent authority does not agree, it may require the manufacturer to provide a report and ensure appropriate follow-up action.
f.applicability: Suspected serious incidents forwarded by a competent authority from healthcare professional, user or patient reports

rows.deadline: Per Article 87(1) to (5) timelines for serious incidents
rows.quote:
Where the manufacturer of the device concerned considers that the incident is a serious incident, it shall provide a report in accordance with paragraphs 1 to 5 of this Article on that serious incident to the competent authority of the Member State in which that serious incident occurred and shall take the appropriate follow-up action in accordance with Article 89.

 Where the manufacturer of the device concerned considers that the incident is not a serious incident or is an expected undesirable side-effect, which will be covered by trend reporting in accordance with Article 88, it shall provide an explanatory statement. If the competent authority does not agree with the conclusion of the explanatory statement, it may require the manufacturer to provide a report in accordance with paragraphs 1 to 5 of this Article and require it to ensure that appropriate follow-up action is taken in accordance with Article 89.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote omits the first subparagraph of Art 87(11) (authority forwards reports to the manufacturer), on which the applicability relies; below 90.

f.title: Report statistically significant increases in non-serious incidents or expected side-effects (trend reporting)
f.statement: Manufacturers shall report, by means of the electronic system referred to in Article 92, any statistically significant increase in the frequency or severity of incidents that are not serious incidents or that are expected undesirable side-effects that could have a significant impact on the benefit-risk analysis referred to in Sections 1 and 5 of Annex I and which have led or may lead to risks to the health or safety of patients, users or other persons that are unacceptable when weighed against the intended benefits. The significant increase shall be established in comparison to the foreseeable frequency or severity of such incidents in respect of the device, or category or group of devices, during a specific period as specified in the technical documentation and product information.
f.legal_basis: MDR Art 88(1); Annex I Sections 1 and 5
f.systems: Electronic system on vigilance and post-market surveillance (Article 92)

rows.quote: 1.   Manufacturers shall report, by means of the electronic system referred to in Article 92, any statistically significant increase in the frequency or severity of incidents that are not serious incidents or that are expected undesirable side-effects that could have a significant impact on the benefit-risk analysis referred to in Sections 1 and 5 of Annex I and which have led or may lead to risks to the health or safety of patients, users or other persons that are unacceptable when weighed against the intended benefits. The significant increase shall be established in comparison to the foreseeable frequency or severity of such incidents in respect of the device, or category or group of devices, in question during a specific period as specified in the technical documentation and product information.

f.title: Investigate reported serious incidents without delay, including a risk assessment of the incident and FSCA
f.statement: Following the reporting of a serious incident pursuant to Article 87(1), the manufacturer shall, without delay, perform the necessary investigations in relation to the serious incident and the devices concerned. This shall include a risk assessment of the incident and field safety corrective action taking into account criteria as referred to in Article 89(3) as appropriate.

f.title: Cooperate with authorities during investigations and do not alter the device or batch sample before informing them

f.statement: The competent authority shall monitor the manufacturer's investigation of a serious incident. Where necessary, a competent authority may intervene in a manufacturer's investigation or initiate an independent investigation.

f.title: Issue a field safety notice without delay, in the required language, submitting the draft to the competent authority
f.statement: The manufacturer shall ensure that information about the field safety corrective action taken is brought without delay to the attention of users of the device by means of a field safety notice. The notice shall be edited in an official Union language or languages determined by the Member State in which the FSCA is taken. Except in cases of urgency, the content of the draft field safety notice shall be submitted to the evaluating competent authority or, in coordinated cases, to the coordinating competent authority to allow it to make comments. Unless duly justified by the situation of the individual Member State, the content of the field safety notice shall be consistent in all Member States.
f.exceptions: Draft submission not required in cases of urgency; content may differ between Member States where duly justified.

rows.deadline: Without delay; draft to the competent authority before issue except in cases of urgency

The field safety notice shall be edited in an official Union language or languages determined by the Member State in which the field safety corrective action is taken. Except in cases of urgency, the content of the draft field safety notice shall be submitted to the evaluating competent authority or, in the cases referred to in paragraph 9, to the coordinating competent authority to allow it to make comments. It shall explain, in a clear manner, without understating the level of risk, the reasons for the FSCA with reference to the device malfunction and associated risks for patients, users or other persons, and shall clearly indicate all the actions to be taken by users.

f.title: Take necessary corrective actions when informed by the authority of a new or changed risk

dates.title: Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR): date of application
dates.scope: Manufacturers, authorised representatives, importers and distributors of medical devices; general date of application (Articles 123(3) derogations aside, e.g. Eudamed-dependent vigilance provisions of Articles 87 and 88)
dates.location: Article 123(2) Entry into force and date of application
dates.timing_note: Date of application in the original 2017 text captured here. Article 123(3)(d) defers Eudamed-related obligations (including Articles 87 and 88) to six months after a Commission notice whose date is not stated. Entry into force (twentieth day after OJ publication) is not recorded because the obligations apply only from this date.

dates.title: MDR: serious adverse event reporting under the Regulation for ongoing directive-based clinical investigations
